info.title: Blue ID & Fisheries Information Management System API
info.description:
The backend for the **Cross River State Blue ID & Fisheries Information Management System** — the
authoritative register of fishermen, boats, engines, cooperatives and government interventions across
the state's 18 Local Government Areas.

---

## Authentication

This API owns authentication end to end. There is **no external identity provider** in the default
configuration: it hashes passwords with Argon2id, issues its own tokens, and handles reset.

### Signing in

```
POST /api/v1/auth/login   { "email": "...", "password": "..." }
```

returns an **access token** and a **refresh token**:

| Token | Lifetime | Stored? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access | short (15m default) | no — stateless JWT | Sent on every request as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| Refresh | long (30d default) | yes, hashed | Exchanged at `/auth/refresh` for a new pair |

The split is deliberate. Access tokens are fast to verify but **cannot be withdrawn**, so they are
short-lived. Refresh tokens are stored precisely so they **can** be withdrawn: suspending an officer,
changing a password or signing out a device all work by revoking them.

### Refresh rotation and theft detection

Every refresh issues a new token and retires the old one. Presenting an already-rotated token
revokes the **entire session family** — the most likely explanation is that it was stolen, and
signing both parties out beats letting an impersonation continue quietly. Treat
`REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID` as "sign in again", never as a transient error to retry.

### Roles come from MongoDB, never from the token

The access token carries identity only — the user id and the session id. Role and scope are re-read
from the database on **every** request, so a demotion, suspension or scope change takes effect on the
next call rather than whenever the token expires. The session named in the token is checked too, so
a sign-out or password change invalidates outstanding access tokens at their next use.

### Account protection

- **8** consecutive failures locks that **account** for **15 minutes** (`423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED`),
  wherever the attempts come from.
- Rate limits come in **two tiers**, because one key cannot do both jobs. An LGA office sits behind a
  single NAT: limit on the IP alone and one officer fumbling their password locks out the whole
  building, which reads as an outage. Limit on the account alone and an attacker rotates accounts
  freely. So login allows **10 attempts per account from one IP per 15 minutes**, under a ceiling of
  **60 attempts from that IP across all accounts**. Password reset is **5 per hour per IP**.
- A **wrong** login returns the **same generic error** whatever the cause, so the endpoint cannot be
  used to discover which addresses are registered. The real reason goes to the audit trail. The one
  exception is a **correct** password on a deactivated account, which answers
  `403 ACCOUNT_INACTIVE` — a suspended officer needs to know why they cannot get in, rather than
  concluding they have forgotten their password.
- `/auth/forgot-password` always reports success for the same reason.

### Who has an account

Only **operators** — the people who run the system. There are 6 roles:

| Role | Capabilities | |
|---|---|---|
| `SUPER_ADMIN` | 4 | Oversight only — creates accounts and reads the audit trail. Holds no operational grant. |
| `STATE_ADMIN` | 24 | Full operational authority state-wide. The role that actually runs the register. |
| `MINISTRY_OFFICER` | 11 | Programmes, verification and reporting. Cannot register or edit a fisherman. |
| `LGA_ADMIN` | 21 | Full operations, confined to their own Local Government Areas. |
| `ENUMERATOR` | 6 | Field registration and offline sync. Cannot verify their own submissions. |
| `COOPERATIVE_OFFICER` | 3 | Their own cooperative and its membership. |

**`SUPER_ADMIN` is deliberately the smallest role, not the largest.** It exists to put the other
accounts in place and to watch what is done with them: it cannot register or edit a fisherman, verify
a registration, issue a Blue ID, move an asset, run a programme, allocate a benefit, or export the
register. Those powers belong to `STATE_ADMIN`. The separation is the point — the account that
creates every other account must not also be able to act under them, or the audit trail it exists to
police becomes a record of its own work.

It still outranks everyone, which is what lets it create a `STATE_ADMIN`. **Rank governs who you may
create; it never governs what you may do.** Every route that gates on rank also gates on a permission.

**Fishermen do not have accounts.** They are the *subject* of records, never users of the API. They
are registered by an officer and identified by their Blue ID.

---

## Three layers of access control

Every request passes through all three:

1. **Capability** — does this role hold the permission the route demands? Listed per operation below.
2. **Scope** — which rows may this user see? Merged into every query inside the service layer, so a
   route cannot forget it. An LGA administrator in Bakassi cannot read Odukpani's register.
3. **Object check** — may this user touch *this* record? Applied after loading. Knowing an id is
   never sufficient.

---

## Response shape

Success:
```json
{ "success": true, "data": { }, "meta": { }, "requestId": "..." }
```

Failure:
```json
{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "details": [] }, "requestId": "..." }
```

**Branch on `error.code`, never on the message text** — messages are written for humans and may
change. Quote `requestId` when reporting a problem; it ties the response to the audit trail.

---

### Error codes



Branch on `error.code`, never on `error.message`: the message is written for a person and may be reworded, the code is the contract.



#### Sign in again

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `TOKEN_MISSING` | 401 | No `Authorization: Bearer` header was sent. |
| `TOKEN_INVALID` | 401 | The token is not one this service issued, or it has been tampered with. |
| `TOKEN_EXPIRED` | 401 | The access token has expired. Call `/auth/refresh` and retry once. |
| `TOKEN_NOT_ACTIVE` | 401 | The token carries a `nbf` in the future — usually a clock skew on the device. |
| `TOKEN_NO_SUBJECT` | 401 | The token has no subject claim, so it identifies nobody. |
| `WRONG_TOKEN_TYPE` | 401 | A refresh token was sent where an access token belongs. They are not interchangeable. |
| `SESSION_REVOKED` | 401 | The session behind this token was ended — by a sign-out, a password change, or a suspension. Sign in again. |
| `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID` | 401 | The refresh token is unknown, already used, or revoked. **A reused token revokes its whole family**, so this can also mean another client refreshed and the session was ended as a suspected theft. |
| `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | 401 | Wrong password, or no such account — deliberately indistinguishable. |
| `ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND` | 401 | The account the token names no longer exists. |
| `WEAK_PASSWORD` | 422 | The password fails the policy. `details` lists every reason at once, so the user fixes them in one attempt rather than discovering them one by one. |
| `RESET_TOKEN_INVALID` | 400 | The reset link is unknown, already used, or past its expiry. Single use by design. |
| `SERVICE_KEY_INVALID` | 401 | The `x-api-key` for a machine-to-machine integration is wrong. |

#### Not permitted — do not retry

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `MISSING_PERMISSION` | 403 | The role does not hold the capability this route requires. |
| `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` | 403 | The account is still on a password it was issued rather than chose. Only the change-password, sign-out and own-profile routes work until it is replaced. |
| `ACCOUNT_INACTIVE` | 403 | Suspended or disabled. Returned on sign-in too, even with the correct password, so the holder knows why. |
| `ACCOUNT_PENDING` | 403 | Created but not yet approved by an administrator. |
| `ACCOUNT_REMOVED` | 403 | The account has been deleted. |
| `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` | 423 | Too many consecutive failures on this account. Wait; it clears itself. |
| `AUTH_FAILURES_EXCEEDED` | 429 | Too many failed authentications from this source. Wait; `Retry-After` says how long. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests. Respect `Retry-After`. |
| `SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN` | 403 | You cannot approve or verify a record you submitted yourself. |
| `SERVICE_READ_ONLY` | 403 | Service credentials are read-only; this route writes. |
| `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` | 403 | Only in external-identity modes: the provider has not verified the address. |
| `USER_NOT_PROVISIONED` | 403 | Only in external-identity modes: no local account is linked to this login. |

#### Rule or state prevents it

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No such record — **or** one outside your scope. The two are deliberately the same answer, so an id cannot be used to probe for records you may not see. |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 422 | Field-level problems; `details` lists them. |
| `DUPLICATE_KEY` | 409 | A unique value is already taken. |
| `STALE_UPDATE` | 409 | Someone changed this record since you loaded it. Reload and retry. |
| `ALREADY_VERIFIED` | 409 | A Blue ID has already been issued — possibly by someone else a moment ago. |
| `DUPLICATE_REVIEW_PENDING` | 409 | An unresolved duplicate flag blocks verification. Resolve it first; this is what stops a duplicate entering the benefit stream. |
| `INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION` | 409 | That status cannot follow the current one. The lifecycle is a state machine: a deceased record cannot become active again, for example. |
| `NOT_VERIFIED` | 409 | The action needs a verified record, and no Blue ID has been issued. |
| `PHOTO_REQUIRED` | 400 | A passport photograph must be attached before a Blue ID can be issued. |
| `BLUE_ID_NOT_ISSUED` | 409 | A QR code cannot exist before the Blue ID it encodes. |
| `NO_VERIFICATION_TOKEN` | 409 | The record has no card token yet — verify it first. |
| `BLUE_ID_REQUIRED` | 400 | A benefit can only be recorded against a verified fisherman. |
| `INVALID_IDENTIFIER` | 400 | The id is not a well-formed identifier. |
| `INVALID_FILTER_VALUE` | 400 | A query filter holds a value the field cannot take. |
| `PAGINATION_TOO_DEEP` | 400 | That page is too far in. Narrow the filters, or use an export. |
| `EMAIL_TAKEN` | 409 | An account already exists with that address. |

#### Programmes and benefits

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ALREADY_ALLOCATED` | 409 | This person already holds a live allocation from this programme. The rule that one benefit is issued once per person per programme. |
| `PROGRAMME_FULL` | 409 | The beneficiary target has been reached. |
| `PROGRAMME_NOT_OPEN` | 409 | The programme is in draft, closed or archived. |
| `PROGRAMME_HAS_ALLOCATIONS` | 409 | Allocations exist, so the programme cannot be deleted — archive it. |
| `NOT_ELIGIBLE` | 422 | The fisherman does not meet the programme criteria. |
| `BENEFICIARY_NOT_ELIGIBLE` | 422 | The named beneficiary fails this programme's eligibility rules — deceased, suspended, wrong LGA, or already served. |
| `ELIGIBILITY_LOCKED` | 409 | Criteria cannot change once allocations have been made against them. |

#### Communities, cooperatives, assets

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `COMMUNITY_EXISTS` | 409 | A community of that name already exists in that LGA. |
| `COMMUNITY_IN_USE` | 409 | Fishermen are registered there; deactivate rather than remove. |
| `COMMUNITY_LGA_MISMATCH` | 400 | The community does not belong to the LGA given. |
| `UNKNOWN_COMMUNITY` | 400 | No such community. |
| `UNKNOWN_LGA` | 400 | Not one of the 18 Local Government Area codes. |
| `COOPERATIVE_IN_USE` | 409 | The society still has members; deactivate rather than remove. |
| `ALREADY_A_MEMBER` | 409 | The fisherman already belongs to another cooperative. |
| `ASSET_ALREADY_REGISTERED` | 409 | That registration number or serial is already on file against another owner — a strong signal of a re-registration attempt. |
| `OWNER_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The fisherman this asset belongs to could not be found. |
| `OWNER_UNRESOLVED` | 422 | The synced record does not say which fisherman it belongs to. |

#### Offline sync and devices

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DEVICE_REQUIRED` | 400 | The route needs an enrolled device; send `x-device-id`. |
| `DEVICE_NOT_REGISTERED` | 403 | That device code is unknown. |
| `DEVICE_NOT_ENROLLED` | 403 | The device has no active enrolment. Re-enrol it. |
| `DEVICE_NOT_ACTIVE` | 403 | The device is suspended or revoked. Takes effect on the next request, not when a token expires. |
| `DEVICE_SECRET_INVALID` | 401 | The device secret does not match. |
| `DEVICE_CODE_TAKEN` | 409 | Another device already uses that code. |
| `SYNC_IN_PROGRESS` | 409 | Another push from this device is still running. Wait rather than retrying immediately. |
| `BATCH_IN_PROGRESS` | 409 | This batch is still being processed. Poll its status; do not resend. |
| `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Split the batch. The limit is `SYNC_MAX_BATCH_SIZE` records. |
| `RECORD_INVALID` | 422 | A record inside the batch failed validation. The batch still completes; the payload is kept so it can be corrected rather than lost. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_ENTITY` | 400 | The batch names an entity type this endpoint does not accept. |

#### Uploads

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `INVALID_IMAGE_CONTENT` | 400 | The bytes are not a recognised image, whatever the filename or content type said. Checked by magic number. |
| `MEDIA_TYPE_MISMATCH` | 400 | The declared content type does not match the actual bytes. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | 415 | That image format is not accepted. |
| `MEDIA_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Media storage is not configured on this instance, so nothing can be uploaded. |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | The body exceeds `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB`. |

#### Transport and server

| Code | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `MALFORMED_JSON` | 400 | The body is not valid JSON. |
| `BAD_REQUEST` | 400 | Generic malformed request. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | Generic authentication failure, where no more specific code applies. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Generic refusal, where no more specific code applies. |
| `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No such endpoint. Check the method and the `/api/v1` prefix. |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 | Generic conflict. |
| `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | The database is unreachable. Retry with backoff. |
| `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | A dependency is unavailable. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Unexpected fault. `requestId` in the body ties it to the server log. |
| `PASSWORD_UNCHANGED` | 400 | The new password is the same as the current one. |

---

## Rate limits

Keyed to your account where one is known, otherwise to your IP. Responses carry
`RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`.

Counters live in the application process, so they are per instance rather than shared. A single
long-running deployment is therefore exact; a horizontally scaled or serverless one allows roughly
the stated budget per instance. That is a deliberate trade for not running a second datastore, and
the per-account lockout — which lives in the database — is the layer that holds regardless.

| Surface | Budget |
|---|---|
| Sign in, per account from one IP | 10 / 15 min |
| Sign in, per IP across all accounts | 60 / 15 min |
| Failed authentications, per identity | 20 / 15 min |
| Password reset | 5 / hour per IP |
| General | 300 / 15 min |
| Sync | 60 / min (deliberately generous — a device back from a week offline pushes many batches) |
| Public verification | 30 / min per IP |
| Exports | 20 / 5 min |

---

## A note on the word "transaction"

Where this documentation says *transaction*, it means a **database transaction** — a group of writes
that either all succeed or all roll back, used so that issuing a Blue ID or recording a benefit
cannot half-happen.

**There is no wallet, payment rail, or money movement anywhere in this system.** Programmes carry a
`unitValue` and allocations carry a `value`, but those are *recorded amounts for budgeting and
reporting*. Recording that someone received a ₦1.85m outboard engine is not the same as paying them,
and this API does not do the latter.

BearerAuth.description:
The **access token** returned by `POST /api/v1/auth/login` or `/auth/refresh`. Short-lived — refresh it rather than extending its life. A refresh token is NOT accepted here and is refused with `WRONG_TOKEN_TYPE`.

In local development with `AUTH_MODE=disabled`, send `x-debug-uid` and `x-debug-role` headers instead.

ServiceApiKey.name: x-api-key
ServiceApiKey.description: Machine-to-machine key for trusted government integrations. **Read-only** — any non-GET request is refused.

DeviceSecret.name: x-device-secret
DeviceSecret.description: Enrolment secret issued when a field device is registered, shown exactly once. Required on every sync push. The device code is an identifier, not a credential.

SuccessEnvelope.description: Every successful response uses this shape.

data.description: The payload. Shape depends on the endpoint.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Every failure uses this shape. Clients MUST branch on `error.code`, never on the message text, which is written for humans and may change.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Examples: UNAUTHENTICATED, TOKEN_EXPIRED, TOKEN_REVOKED, ACCOUNT_PENDING, ACCOUNT_INACTIVE, MISSING_PERMISSION, PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED, NOT_FOUND, VALIDATION_ERROR, CONFLICT, DUPLICATE_KEY, STALE_UPDATE, INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION, DUPLICATE_REVIEW_PENDING, ALREADY_ALLOCATED, PROGRAMME_FULL, BENEFICIARY_NOT_ELIGIBLE, RATE_LIMITED, DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE.

requestId.description: Echoes the x-request-id header. Quote it when reporting a problem — it ties the response to the audit trail.

total.description: Null when counting would have been too slow; `hasNextPage` is still accurate.

countUnavailable.description: Present only when the total was skipped.

GeoPoint.description: GeoJSON Point. Coordinates are [longitude, latitude] — in that order.

accuracy.description: Metres, as reported by the device.

Media.description: An image stored in Cloudinary with `authenticated` delivery. `url` is a SHORT-LIVED SIGNED URL and expires — re-request it rather than caching it.

phone.description: Nigerian mobile number in any common format.

Fisherman.description: A person in the register. `nin` and the internal matching keys are never serialised; `ninMasked` appears only for callers holding `fisherman:read_sensitive`.

blueId.description: Permanent identifier, issued ONLY on verification. Absent while the record is pending. Format: <state>-<segment>-<LGA>-<sequence>.

tempReference.description: Printed on the paper slip given in the field before a Blue ID exists.

estimatedYearOfBirth.description: Used where an exact date is unknown, which is common in the field.

ninMasked.description: Only for `fisherman:read_sensitive` holders. The full value needs `?includeNin=true` and is audited.

fishermanTypes.description: A person may hold several at once, e.g. boat owner AND artisanal fisher.

capturedAt.description: When the enumerator captured it, which may be days before it synced.

qrVersion.description: Incremented on every card reissue; an older card stops validating.

FishermanCreate.description: Authority fields (blueId, status, verification, duplicateFlags) are STRIPPED if sent — they cannot be assigned by a client. One of `dateOfBirth` or `estimatedYearOfBirth` is required.

nin.description: Optional. Stored encrypted; never returned in full without the sensitive grant.

DuplicateFlag.description: A suspected duplicate held for human review. Records are NEVER merged or deleted automatically.

isDuplicate.description: True when the score meets the configured threshold.

canoeType.description: Local classification, which varies by community.

allocation.description: Set when the boat arrived through a government programme.

boat.description: Optional: an engine may be owned without being fitted.

serialNumber.description: Unique state-wide. This is what lets the ministry answer "was this engine already issued to someone else?".

Equipment.description: Nets, cold boxes, ice boxes, safety kit, GPS units and smoking kilns. Counted rather than individually identified.

facilities.description: Drives the "which communities lack cold storage / landing sites / boat repair" reports.

Programme.description: A government intervention. Eligibility is machine-readable so beneficiary lists can be pre-screened rather than compiled by hand.

unitValue.description: Value of one unit, for budgeting and reporting. NOT a payment instruction — this API moves no money.

Eligibility.description: Criteria evaluated server-side. Encoding them as data is what allows "who qualifies?" to be answered as a query.

excludeIfReceivedWithinMonths.description: Blocks a person who received the same PROGRAMME TYPE within this window. The main defence against collecting one intervention twice.

Allocation.description: A benefit issued to one Blue ID holder under one programme. One ACTIVE allocation per person per programme is enforced by a database index.

value.description: Recorded value of the item issued. Informational — no funds are transferred by this API.

isActiveAllocation.description: Derived from status; the uniqueness index filters on it.

acknowledgement.description: Proof of collection captured at handover.

User.description: A portal/field-app OPERATOR — not a fisherman. Fishermen have no accounts; they are the subject of records, identified by their Blue ID. This service owns the credential: the password hash lives on this record and is never returned. The record also carries the role and geographic scope, which are re-read on every request so a demotion or suspension takes effect immediately.

authUid.description: External identity-provider subject. Null in the default local mode, which is what this deployment runs; only used when AUTH_MODE is jwt or jwks.

scope.description: Which LGAs and communities this operator may act in. Empty LGAs on a state-wide role means all.

permissions.description: Resolved capabilities, so the portal can render menus without a second call.

Device.description: An enrolled field device. Every offline record carries the device it was captured on.

clientRecordId.description: Generated ON THE DEVICE when the enumerator saves, before the server has ever seen the record. This is the idempotency key: a replayed batch updates the same row instead of creating a second person.

data.description: The record payload. Validated per entity at apply time; authority fields (blueId, status, verification) are stripped. Assets may reference their owner by `ownerClientRecordId` when the server id is not yet known.

clientRevision.description: Incremented by the device on each local edit; used to detect conflicts.

baseUpdatedAt.description: The server `updatedAt` the device last saw.

clientBatchId.description: Identifies the push. Re-sending the same id returns the ORIGINAL outcome rather than reprocessing.

deviceCode.description: May also be sent as the x-device-id header.

deviceSecret.description: May also be sent as the x-device-secret header. Required.

replayed.description: True when this batch was already processed and the stored result is being returned.

results.description: Per-record outcome. The device uses this to mark records synced, show a correction, or retry.

changes.description: Records changed since the supplied cursors, keyed by entity.

deletions.description: Tombstones, so a device stops showing a withdrawn registration.

cursors.description: PER-ENTITY cursors. Send these back on the next pull. A single shared cursor would skip records, because entities drain at different rates.

VerificationResult.description: Disclosure is tiered. Without a session: identity and status only. A signed-in officer may request `detailed=true` for assets, cooperative and benefit history.

message.example: This Blue ID is valid and active.

photo.description: Signed URL. Released only to a signed-in officer.

AuditEntry.description: Append-only. Updates and deletes are rejected by the data layer.

changes.description: Field-level diff. Whole snapshots are deliberately not stored — they would multiply copies of personal data.

PermissionList.description: Capability names used by the authorization layer.

NotFound.description: The record does not exist — **or** is outside your scope. The two are deliberately indistinguishable, because confirming existence would itself disclose information.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state. Codes: `DUPLICATE_KEY`, `ALREADY_VERIFIED`, `ALREADY_ALLOCATED`, `PROGRAMME_FULL`, `INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION`, `DUPLICATE_REVIEW_PENDING`, `STALE_UPDATE`.

ValidationError.description: The body or query failed validation. `error.details` lists the offending fields.

Unavailable.description: A dependency is unavailable. Code: `DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE`. Retry shortly.

get.description: Confirms the process is running. Touches no dependency, so a slow database never causes a restart of a healthy server.

Reports whether this instance can serve traffic.

Anonymous callers receive **up/down only**. The detailed body names internal collections, integration state and any missing database constraints, so it is released only to a caller presenting `x-probe-key`.

Fails (503) when MongoDB is unreachable, when a critical index is missing, or during graceful shutdown (`draining`).

parameters.name: x-probe-key
parameters.description: Internal probe key. Without it the response is `{status}` only.

503.description: Not ready, or draining during shutdown.

get.description: Lists the available endpoint groups. Useful as a connectivity check.
Every enumeration the portal and field app build dropdowns from, plus the 18 Cross River LGAs and the Blue ID format. Clients should read vocabularies from here rather than hard-coding them.

Resolves the bearer token to this operator's record, role, geographic scope and derived permissions. The portal calls this immediately after sign-in.

Role and scope are read from MongoDB on every request — never from the token — so a demotion or suspension takes effect on the next call rather than when the token expires.

patch.description: Self-service. Role, scope and status cannot be changed here — that would be privilege escalation.

get.description:
Administrators see only staff working in their own LGAs.

**Requires:** `user:manage`

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Deep offsets are refused past ~10,000 skipped documents; narrow the filters or export instead.

post.description:
Creates the account **with a credential** and emails an invitation.

Omit `password` and the system generates a temporary one, returned **once** in this response as `temporaryPassword` and never recoverable afterwards. Pass it to the officer by whatever channel you trust; it is not emailed.

Either way the account is flagged `mustChangePassword` — a generated one because nobody has chosen it yet, an administrator-supplied one because the administrator knows it. Until the holder replaces it their sign-in reaches only `/auth/change-password`, `/auth/logout`, `/auth/logout-all`, `/auth/sessions` and `/users/me`; everything else answers `403 PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED`. That is enforced server-side, not left to the client.

You cannot create a role at or above your own, or assign an LGA outside your own scope. `SUPER_ADMIN` can therefore never be created here — it exists only via the server-side bootstrap command.

**Requires:** `user:manage`

201.description: Account created. A generated password appears here once.

temporaryPassword.description: Present only when the system generated it. Shown once; not recoverable.

get.description:
The account, its role and its geographic scope. Credential fields are never returned.

**Requires:** `user:manage`

patch.description:
Role and scope changes are privileged and cannot escalate. You cannot change your own role.

**Requires:** `user:manage`

post.description:
Activates an account that was auto-provisioned on first sign-in, assigning its role and scope.

**Requires:** `user:manage`

patch.description:
Suspending revokes every live session for the account immediately, so an access token already in someone's hands stops working on its next request rather than when it expires. The status is re-read on every request, which is what makes that true.

You cannot change your own status, or the status of an account at or above your own role.

**Requires:** `user:manage`

get.description:
`search` accepts a Blue ID, a phone number (any Nigerian format) or a name. A name search uses the text index; an NIN is matched through its blind index.

post.summary: Verify and issue the Blue ID
post.description:
The **only** path that mints a Blue ID. Runs in a database transaction: the sequence is allocated and the record claimed atomically, so concurrent verifications cannot issue two numbers or burn one.

Refuses when: a Blue ID already exists, a duplicate review is still open, or no photograph has been uploaded.

**Separation of duties:** you cannot verify a record you registered yourself.

**Requires:** `registration:verify`

patch.description:
Transitions are enforced by a state machine:

- `PENDING_VERIFICATION` → ACTIVE (only via verification), DUPLICATE_UNDER_REVIEW, INACTIVE, DECEASED
- `ACTIVE` → SUSPENDED, INACTIVE, DECEASED, DUPLICATE_UNDER_REVIEW
- `SUSPENDED` → ACTIVE, INACTIVE, DECEASED
- `INACTIVE` → ACTIVE, DECEASED
- `DUPLICATE_UNDER_REVIEW` → INACTIVE, DECEASED (release it by *resolving the review*, not by editing status)
- `DECEASED` → **terminal**

An invalid move returns 409 `INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION`.

**Requires:** `registration:status`

post.description:
Submits a batch of records captured without a network.

**Always returns 2xx when the batch is accepted for processing, even if individual records fail** — the per-record outcomes are the payload. A non-2xx would make the device retry the whole batch including records already stored.

**Idempotency.** `clientBatchId` identifies the push: re-sending it returns the original result rather than reprocessing. `clientRecordId` identifies each record: every write is an upsert on it, so a retry after a dropped connection updates the same row instead of creating a second fisherman.

**Device authentication is required** — the device code is an identifier, the secret is the credential (header `x-device-secret` or body `deviceSecret`).

**Nothing is lost.** Rejected records are retained server-side with their payload and field-level errors, retrievable from the rejected-records endpoint.

Records are applied fishermen-first, so assets can resolve their owner. An asset whose owner synced in an earlier batch is matched by `ownerClientRecordId`.

**Requires:** `sync:submit`

403.description: Device suspended or revoked, or the role lacks sync:submit.

409.description: This batch is still being processed.

post.description:
Exchanges sign-in details for an access token and a refresh token.

**Send either `userId` or `email`.** The portal's administration section asks for "User ID" and Password, because that is what an officer is handed; accounts created by invitation are identified by their email address. Both work on this endpoint. The `userId` lookup is case-insensitive.

**A wrong password and an unknown address answer identically** — same status, same code, same message. Distinguishing them would turn this endpoint into an account-enumeration oracle, telling an attacker which government addresses are registered. The real reason is written to the audit trail, where an administrator can see it.

The one exception is a **correct** password on a deactivated account, which answers `403 ACCOUNT_INACTIVE` rather than the generic failure. A suspended officer needs to know why they cannot sign in, or they conclude they have forgotten their password and the reset will not help them. A wrong password on that same account is still indistinguishable from any other failure.

**Lockout and rate limits, in three layers.** Eight consecutive failures hold that *account* shut for 15 minutes and return `423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED`, wherever the attempts come from. On top of that, this endpoint allows 10 attempts per *account from one IP* per 15 minutes, under a ceiling of 60 attempts from that IP across all accounts — two tiers, because an LGA office is behind one NAT and a single key would either lock out the whole building or let an attacker rotate accounts freely. Exceeding either returns `429`.

**Temporary credentials.** If `mustChangePassword` is true the sign-in succeeded, but the token it returned is good for only five routes — changing the password, listing and ending sessions, and reading your own profile. Everything else answers `403 PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` until a password is chosen. This applies to every role, SUPER_ADMIN included.

schema.description: Exactly one of `userId` or `email` is required.

userId.description: The staff identifier the portal labels "User ID". Case-insensitive.

byUserId.summary: Administration section — User ID and password

byEmail.summary: An invited officer — email and password

refreshToken.description: Opaque, long-lived. Store securely; it is rotated on every use.

mustChangePassword.description: True when this account is using a password it was issued rather than one it chose. The restriction is enforced by the server, not by the client: while it is true, every endpoint except `POST /auth/change-password`, `POST /auth/logout`, `POST /auth/logout-all`, `GET /auth/sessions` and `GET /users/me` returns `403 PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED`, whatever the role. Route straight to a change-password screen.

401.description: Generic failure — code `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`. Do not infer anything further from it.

403.description: Account is suspended (`ACCOUNT_INACTIVE`) or awaiting approval (`ACCOUNT_PENDING`).

423.description: Locked after repeated failures. `details.until` carries the release time.

post.description:
Exchanges a refresh token for a **new pair**, retiring the old token.

**Reuse detection.** Presenting a token that has already been rotated means something is wrong — most likely it was captured and the thief is racing the legitimate client. The entire session family is then revoked, signing both parties out. A surprise sign-out is a far better outcome than a silent impersonation, so treat a `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID` here as "sign in again", not as a transient error to retry.

Always store the **new** refresh token from the response; the one you sent is dead.

refreshToken.description: Opaque, long-lived. Store securely; it is rotated on every use.

mustChangePassword.description: True when this account is using a password it was issued rather than one it chose. The restriction is enforced by the server, not by the client: while it is true, every endpoint except `POST /auth/change-password`, `POST /auth/logout`, `POST /auth/logout-all`, `GET /auth/sessions` and `GET /users/me` returns `403 PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED`, whatever the role. Route straight to a change-password screen.

401.description: Invalid, expired, revoked or **reused** token — code `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID`.

403.description: The account is no longer active.

post.description:
Revokes the supplied refresh token. **Idempotent** — an unknown or already-revoked token still returns success, so a client can always clear its state.

The access token is stateless and remains cryptographically valid until it expires, but it is tied to this session and will be refused on its next use.
Revokes every session for the caller, on every device. The usual response to losing a phone.

get.description: Where this account is currently signed in — IP, user agent, device and last use — so an officer can spot a session they do not recognise.

post.description:
Requires the **current** password even though you are already authenticated: an unattended signed-in session should not be enough to take the account over permanently.

Every other session is signed out afterwards, because changing a password is the usual response to suspecting one is compromised. The caller keeps the session they used.

Minimum 12 characters. The password may not contain your own name or email local-part, and may not be a known-common choice.

422.description: The new password was rejected — `WEAK_PASSWORD`, with each problem listed in `details`.

post.description:
Emails a single-use reset link valid for 30 minutes.

**Always reports success**, even for an address with no account — saying "no such user" would let anyone test which government addresses are registered. Do not use the response to decide whether an account exists; it cannot tell you.

Limited to 5 requests per IP per hour.

200.description: Always returned, regardless of whether the address exists.

post.description:
Sets a new password using the token from the emailed link.

The token is **single-use** and cleared on success, so a link captured from an inbox cannot be replayed. Every existing session is revoked, since a reset is how someone recovers a compromised account.

200.description: Password set. Sign in with it.

400.description: The link is invalid, already used or expired — `RESET_TOKEN_INVALID`.

post.description:
Issues a **temporary password, returned once** and flagged `mustChangePassword`. Every session for that account is revoked.

Until the holder sets their own password their next sign-in is confined to the change-password flow — the reset cannot be used to hand somebody a working credential they never replace.

Use this when an officer cannot access their email. Share the password through a channel the person can verify — it is not emailed, and it will not be shown again.

**Requires:** `user:manage`
